_contract.why: The POS lens found THREE definitions of 'below par' on one page. The /inventory chip counted 9 with '2 critical'; GET /inventory/:rid/low-stock counted 7; GET /inventory/:rid/summary reported criticalCount 0 — while the alert service, at the same instant, was calling a wine at 2/5 'critical'. Three answers to one question, on one screen, about the same rows.
_contract.rule: below par means stock_live < threshold_min — STRICTLY below, matching v_low_stock_items, which is the predicate that already decides whether an alert fires. A wine sitting exactly at par is 'at par': the system will not act on it, so no counter may claim it needs acting on. Over-reporting is the same fault as under-reporting, pointed the other way.
_contract.bands: ratio = stock / par. critical: ratio <= 0.5. low: 0.5 < ratio < 1. at_par: ratio == 1. healthy: ratio > 1. unknown: stock is null — MUST NOT read as out of stock.
read_by: apps/web/src/lib/inventoryStatus.ts (SPA: KPI chip, row badges, filters)
_contract.drift: Both suites run THIS file. Add a case here, never to one suite alone — the two implementations are in different languages and nothing else stops them diverging again.
_contract.the_open_question: Whether a wine exactly AT par should count as below par is a judgement about reorder policy, not about code, and it is not written in .planning/decisions/. It is expressed here as one line (at_par is not in below_par_bands) precisely so reversing it is one edit in one file rather than a hunt through three.
